Deal flow is heavy (Perella Weinberg, AMD/World Labs, Xeris, Sangoma) and AI remains the dominant tech story ahead of Micron's earnings.
self_check: My record is roughly a coin flip overall, with rate calls working (4 of 5) and merger-rumor trades mostly failing (1 of 5), so today I lean on the macro rate/oil themes and a defense contract with hard dollars attached, keeping speculative deal chatter to one medium-sized idea.

top_buys.pitch: A $20.7 billion missile contract locks in years of demand as the Pentagon rebuilds stockpiles.
top_buys.why: The Pentagon awarded RTX's Raytheon unit one of the largest AMRAAM contracts ever, driven by depleted inventories after sustained Middle East conflict. That gives multi-year production visibility and likely higher margins as volumes scale. Ongoing Israel-Hamas strikes and US-Iran tension make further munitions orders plausible rather than a one-off.
top_buys.risks: A genuine US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough could cool defense sentiment, and RTX has a history of program execution and supply-chain hiccups.
top_buys.watch: Follow-on munitions awards and RTX's next quarterly guidance on defense backlog conversion.

top_buys.pitch: Wall Street now sees Meta's AI shopping agent taking revenue from Apple and Google.
top_buys.why: A Bank of America note said Meta's Muse shopping agent could drain the most profitable part of Apple's services business, and Apple fell 2% on it while Meta was framed as the beneficiary. That reframes Meta's heavy AI spending as offense rather than cost. Meta also has the ad infrastructure to monetize agentic shopping quickly.
top_buys.risks: Analyst speculation is not revenue, and if the AI trade cracks, as Michael Burry is betting, high-capex names like Meta sell off first.
top_buys.watch: Any concrete launch details or monetization numbers for Meta's shopping agent, and Q3 earnings commentary on AI capex.

top_buys.pitch: A long-term supply deal with Petrobras adds contracted cash flow in a tight energy market.
top_buys.why: Cheniere signed a multi-year LNG sale and purchase agreement with Brazil's Petrobras, the kind of take-or-pay contract that underpins its dividend and buyback. With WTI above $90 and Middle East supply risk in focus, global buyers are keen to lock in US gas. Cheniere's earnings are less sensitive to daily price swings than producers'.
top_buys.risks: A US-Iran de-escalation could soften energy prices broadly, and long-dated contracts add little near-term earnings.
top_buys.watch: Further SPA announcements and updates on train expansion timelines.

top_buys.pitch: Takeover talk from Piper Sandler lands in the middle of a very busy M&A market.
top_buys.why: Shares surged on a report that Piper Sandler is in talks to buy the advisory boutique, which would carry a control premium. Today's headline flow, from AMD's $8.2 billion World Labs deal to Sangoma and SoundThinking buyouts, shows an active deal cycle that also lifts Perella's core advisory fees. Even without a deal, the fee backdrop is improving.
top_buys.risks: Deal reports often fizzle, and my recent merger-rumor picks have mostly not worked; a denial could erase the pop quickly.
top_buys.watch: Confirmation or denial from Piper Sandler or Perella Weinberg in the coming days.

top_buys.pitch: WTI above $90 with Middle East supply risk keeps upstream cash flow strong.
top_buys.why: Analysts note that crude above $90 comfortably supports Exxon's growth plans, helped by low-cost Permian barrels and Guyana discoveries. Oil is being held up by supply worries tied to Iran and the US exit from Iraq. Exxon converts high prices into buybacks and dividends faster than most peers.
top_buys.risks: Renewed US-Iran talks and possible sanctions relief could knock crude lower quickly, and this call went against me last week.
top_buys.watch: Headlines on US-Iran negotiations and weekly US crude inventory data.
